question: What is the main purpose of diluting a medicated lotion?

options.B: To change the color of the medication
options.C: To extend the physical shelf life indefinitely

explanation: Dilution reduces the strength of the active drug to make it safer for sensitive skin or large areas. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why might a nurse dilute a topical steroid for a pediatric patient?

options.A: Pediatric patients require higher drug dosages
options.B: Pediatric skin lacks a normal epidermal layer
options.C: Children refuse to use unmixed topical creams
options.D: Children absorb drugs faster through delicate skin

explanation: Young children have thinner skin which increases systemic absorption risks, making lower concentrations necessary. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h1)

question: What happens when chemically incompatible topical bases are mixed together?

options.A: Immediate evaporation of the active ingredient
options.B: Phase separation and uneven drug distribution
options.C: Solidification into a hard protective barrier
options.D: Enhancement of the total therapeutic potency

explanation: Incompatible bases will separate, meaning the patient will not get an even dose of medicine. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which diluent characteristic is most important when mixing a water-based lotion?

options.B: Bright coloration for easy visual tracking
options.C: Compatibility with the primary emulsion base

explanation: The diluent must match the base formulation to ensure the mixture stays smoothly blended. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h2)

question: How much active lotion is needed to make a 1:1 dilution with 50ml of vehicle?
explanation: A 1:1 dilution requires equal parts of both substances, so 50ml of active lotion matches 50ml of vehicle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h3)

question: What formula format helps nurses calculate custom topical drug dilutions safely?

options.A: Intravenous drip rate drop factor equations

explanation: Dilution calculations rely on balancing concentration and volume ratios to find the right amounts. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why is geometric dilution or thorough spatula blending necessary during compounding?

options.A: To activate the preservatives inside the commercial lotion
options.B: To speed up the natural evaporation of water content
options.C: To ensure uniform distribution of the active drug
options.D: To change the chemical structure of the steroid base

explanation: Thorough mixing prevents hot spots where the drug is too concentrated in one part of the bottle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing a diluted lotion on a hospital tray. What is the very first step?

options.A: Apply the mixed lotion directly onto the patient's back
options.B: Pour the active medication directly into a large basin
options.C: Sanitize the workspace and put on clean gloves
options.D: Calculate the patient's daily fluid intake requirements

explanation: Infection control requires a clean work surface and proper barrier protection before handling drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h4)

question: What critical detail must be written on the label of a freshly diluted lotion?

options.A: Manufacturer name of the original raw chemical
options.B: Date of compounding and new expiration date
options.C: Specific batch number of the hospital laundry soap
options.D: Patient's exact room number and bed designation

explanation: Diluted products spoil quickly, so clear preparation and expiry dates prevent the use of degraded drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h5)

question: Why do home-diluted topical lotions have a much shorter shelf life?

options.A: Commercial preservatives become diluted and less effective
options.B: Exposure to oxygen permanently solidifies the base oil
options.C: Hospital room temperatures destroy active steroid molecules
options.D: Plastifiers from the storage container leach into the cream

explanation: Adding extra vehicle weakens the preservative system, allowing bacteria and fungi to grow rapidly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h5)

question: A nurse is about to apply a diluted steroid lotion to a patient's forearm. What should the nurse check first?

options.A: Skin integrity and presence of open wounds
options.B: The patient's current blood pressure reading
options.C: The exact weight of the container in grams
options.D: Whether the patient has eaten breakfast yet

explanation: Applying certain topical agents over broken skin can cause pain, excessive systemic absorption, or irritation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h6)

question: In which direction should a nurse smooth topical lotions onto a patient's skin?

options.A: In the direction of hair growth
options.C: Against the natural grain of the skin
options.D: Upwards toward the nearest lymph node

explanation: Smoothing lotions in the direction of hair growth prevents painful inflammation of the hair follicles. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is the primary danger of storing diluted lotions in recycled food containers?

options.A: Accidental ingestion by children or household members
options.B: Chemical reactions between the food residue and plastic
options.C: Complete evaporation of the active pharmaceutical base
options.D: Rapid freezing of the emulsion in home refrigerators

explanation: Putting medicine in food containers creates a serious poisoning risk if someone mistakes it for food or drink. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h7)

question: Which practice directly prevents calculation and compounding mistakes during lotion dilution?

options.A: Extending the expiration date past standard safety guidelines
options.B: Using household spoons to measure liquid ingredients
options.C: Leaving the compounded container unlabeled on a bedside table
options.D: Having a colleague double-check the math and measurements

explanation: Independent double-checking catches mathematical and measuring errors before the preparation reaches the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h7)
